newsitem.title: ITALY: No extension allowed for Italy TV decree-minister.
newsitem.headline: No extension allowed for Italy TV decree-minister.

text.p: A cabinet decree which allows the current framework for Italian television stations to run until January 31, 1997 will not be extended beyond this date, Post and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico said on Wednesday.

The decree was approved by cabinet earlier on Wednesday and plugs a legal void caused by a 1994 constitutional court ruling which said no single private proprietor should be allowed to keep three television channels after August 27, 1996.
Former prime minister and centre-right leader Silvio Berlusconi controls three national television channels.
Italy's centre-left government presented new legislation on television ownership in July and Maccanico said this would have to be ratified by the January 31 deadline.
"If the bill is not passed into law...the court ruling will come into force," Maccanico told a press conference.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's proposed bill demands that Berlusconi's Mediaset company converts one of its three TV networks into a satellite or cable station by August 1997. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
